policy: Every entry must be Public Domain or Creative Commons (see CLAUDE.md, Corpus licensing). Source: Mutopia Project (mutopiaproject.org) only, for now -- it is the one of the three approved sources (IMSLP, Musopen, ccMixter) that publishes MIDI directly, per-piece, with an explicit machine-readable license field. IMSLP/Musopen/ccMixter become relevant again once the audio front end exists (see README Roadmap); today the pipeline consumes MIDI, so the corpus is MIDI.
baseline_note: baseline_hard/baseline_strain are the UNARRANGED source's violation counts against baseline_profile, from arranger.verify -- i.e. how far a piece is from playable before any arrangement happens. They are a difficulty proxy, not a difficulty score: they change if profiles/me.json changes, and they say nothing about melodic/harmonic difficulty, only physical playability of the raw MIDI. Measured 2026-08-23 against arranger @ 1029cea.
excluded_by_design: Multi-movement works whose MIDI ships only inside a *-mids.zip are no longer excluded as of the entries below -- fetch_corpus.py accepts zip_url + zip_member (stdlib zipfile, see evals/corpus/README.md). Clementi's Sonatina Op.36 No.1 (piece-info id 804) and Grieg's 'Anitra's Dance' Op.46 No.3 (piece-info id 281) were the original candidates skipped before that support existed; neither has been added since -- not a technical limitation now, just nothing has needed them yet.
hard_pool_note: beethoven-piano-concerto3-1, beethoven-violin-concerto-1, and tchaikovsky-op35-2 (last 3 entries below) are not part of the original 20-piece base corpus -- they're the verdict-eligible pool for the 'does the agent beat brute force' investigation in docs/build-log/eval-protocol.md, the only 3 (of 19 candidates measured) whose brute_force_baseline cost is nonzero. See evals/corpus/README.md, 'Sourcing criteria' section, for the full search and the pieces that didn't qualify.

pieces.title: Sonatine
pieces.notes: Early-classical teaching sonatina. Verifier-clean unarranged; good smoke-test piece.

pieces.title: Invention No. 4 in D minor
pieces.notes: Two-part invention, contrapuntal hand independence rather than chordal difficulty.

pieces.title: La Candeur
pieces.notes: 25 Etudes faciles et progressives -- first study in the set, easiest tier.

pieces.title: L'Arabesque
pieces.notes: Well-known progressive study; running RH figuration over a simple LH.

pieces.title: Innocence
pieces.notes: Progressive study, mid-easy tier of the Op.100 set.

pieces.title: La Gracieuse
pieces.notes: Progressive study; one hard violation unarranged, useful minimal-repair test case.

pieces.title: Tendre Fleur
pieces.notes: Progressive study, mid tier of the Op.100 set.

pieces.title: L'Adieu
pieces.notes: Progressive study, upper-middle tier of the Op.100 set.

pieces.title: Ballade
pieces.notes: Hardest of the Op.100 pieces included here; dramatic octave writing.

pieces.title: Prelude ('Funeral March')
pieces.notes: Short, but wide sustained block chords -- good hand_span violation source.

pieces.title: Gymnopédie No. 2
pieces.notes: Slow, but sustained-pedal wide LH voicings read as hard span/leap violations unarranged -- a real example of the pedal-modelling gap in docs/build-log/limitations.md.

pieces.title: Morning Prayer
pieces.notes: Written as a children's teaching piece; simplest entry in the corpus.

pieces.title: Old French Song
pieces.notes: Shortest piece in the corpus; useful as a fast smoke test.

pieces.title: Träumerei (Kinderszenen)
pieces.notes: Famous, harmonically rich; wide inner voicing produces real hard violations unarranged -- a genuine reduction test rather than a straightforward pass-through.

pieces.title: Sonata No. 16 in C major ('Sonata facile'), I. Allegro
pieces.attribution: Typeset for Mutopia by Alejandro Sierra
pieces.notes: CC-BY-SA, not Public Domain -- keep the attribution line if this piece's arrangement is ever redistributed. First movement only; movements 2-3 exist at K545-2/K545-3 if the corpus grows.

pieces.title: Für Elise
pieces.notes: This is the same piece as samples/Fur Elise.mid (gitignored, ungoverned), but a different, licensed, checksummed edition. Prefer this entry going forward; the old file has no provenance.

pieces.title: Waltz No. 15 in A-flat major
pieces.notes: The famous one. Real unarranged hard violations -- genuine reduction candidate.

pieces.title: Impromptu in G-flat major
pieces.notes: The hardest piece in the corpus by baseline violations. Also the one MIDI here with 6 tracks rather than the usual 3 -- io._assign_staves only infers hands from exactly 2 note-carrying tracks, so this file is a real trigger for the staff-assignment gap noted in the M8-era codebase review. Good regression fixture for that specifically.

pieces.title: Solace: A Mexican Serenade
pieces.notes: Only non-European-classical entry -- ragtime syncopation, large stride LH. By far the most violations unarranged; deliberately included as a stress case, the same role Bohemian Rhapsody plays in samples/ but with clean licensing.

pieces.title: Nocturne No. 5 in B-flat major
pieces.attribution: Typeset for Mutopia by Alex Schreiber
pieces.notes: CC-BY-SA, not Public Domain -- keep the attribution line if redistributed. Field effectively invented the nocturne form Chopin later popularised; good precursor-genre entry.

pieces.title: Piano Concerto No. 3 in C minor, I. Allegro con brio
pieces.notes: Full orchestra + solo piano, 14 MIDI tracks. One of only 3 pieces (of 19 measured) whose brute_force_baseline cost is nonzero (3.00, best plan block/voices=2/fold=0) -- see evals/corpus/README.md, 'Sourcing criteria' section. Large file; brute_force_baseline() takes several minutes against it.

pieces.title: Violin Concerto in D major, I. (movement)
pieces.notes: Full orchestra + solo violin, 14 MIDI tracks. brute_force_baseline cost 2.00 (best plan block/voices=1/fold=12) -- see evals/corpus/README.md, 'Sourcing criteria' section. Largest file in the corpus by note count; brute_force_baseline() takes several minutes against it.

pieces.title: Violin Concerto in D major, Op. 35 -- movement 2 (per archive file numbering)
pieces.notes: Full orchestra + solo violin, 16 MIDI tracks. brute_force_baseline cost 4.00 (best plan block/voices=1/fold=12) -- one of only 3 pieces (of 19 measured) that resist. The archive's unlabelled tchai_op35.mid (densest file, cost 5.00) was deliberately excluded from this pool -- its relationship to this file was never established (same zip, plausibly overlapping content), and both cannot safely count as independent votes in a 3-piece verdict pool. See docs/build-log/eval-protocol.md, 2026-08-24 amendment. Also unconfirmed: whether the archive's numbered '1'/'2' files correspond to the concerto's actual movement order -- tchai_op35-1.mid (not in this manifest) is too sparse to plausibly be the real first movement.
